pluss::note::empty_like¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::empty_like(const Note& like)

Another Note’s Shape, Filled With The Empty String¶

empty_like() returns a fresh Note shaped exactly like like, with every cell holding "". It is full_like(like, "").

Use it to stage a same-shaped scratch buffer next to a Note you already have — a place to write transformed rows without disturbing the source, an output grid congruent with the input, a reset copy. Every cell is a valid empty string, so the result works with every Note method immediately; cells you have not written yet simply read as "".

Only the shape of like is used. Its contents and its encoding are ignored — empty_like always produces a UTF-8-mode Note. For a bytes-mode result, use empty_bytes_like.

like must be a defined Note. The result is independent of like.

Example 1: A Same-Shaped Blank Buffer¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
const pluss::Note blank = pluss::note::empty_like(grid);
std::cout << blank << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", "", ""], 
  ["", "", ""]
]

Shape [2, 3] borrowed from grid; every cell reset to "".

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::empty: supply the shape as an explicit sizes list instead.

  • pluss::note::full_like: choose a non-empty fill value.

  • pluss::note::empty_bytes_like: the bytes-mode counterpart.
